nodes.summary: For isomorphic graphs, every verifier and every test $T$ of its view, the rewinding simulator with $k$ attempts (which never sees the isomorphism) and the real interaction pass $T$ with probabilities that differ by at most $2^{-k}$.
nodes.title: Zero knowledge of the graph-isomorphism protocol against an arbitrary verifier, one round

nodes.summary: For simple graphs $G_0$ and $G_1$ on the same vertex type, there is a permutation of the vertices mapping $G_0$ onto $G_1$ if and only if $G_0$ and $G_1$ are isomorphic in Mathlib's sense. So the witnesses of the graph-isomorphism protocol exist exactly for isomorphic pairs.
nodes.title: Witnesses are isomorphisms

nodes.summary: From answers $\sigma$ to a challenge $\alpha$ and $\sigma'$ to a challenge $\alpha'$, the extractor outputs $\sigma_1^{-1} \circ \sigma_0$, where $\sigma_0$ is the answer to the challenge $0$ and $\sigma_1$ the answer to the challenge $1$ (that is, $\sigma^{-1} \circ \sigma'$ if $\alpha = 1$ and $\sigma'^{-1} \circ \sigma$ otherwise).
nodes.title: The extractor

nodes.summary: If $G_0$ and $G_1$ are not isomorphic, no permutation maps $G_0$ onto $G_1$: the statement $(G_0, G_1)$ of the graph-isomorphism protocol has no witness.
nodes.title: Non-isomorphic graphs have no witness

nodes.summary: If $\sigma_0$ maps $G_0$ onto $H$ and $\sigma_1$ maps $G_1$ onto $H$, then $\sigma_1^{-1} \circ \sigma_0$ maps $G_0$ onto $G_1$.
nodes.title: Two answers give an isomorphism

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on $V$ and permutations $\sigma, \tau$ of $V$, relabelling $G$ by $\sigma$ and then by $\tau$ is relabelling it by $\tau \circ \sigma$.
nodes.title: Composing relabellings

nodes.summary: Relabelling a simple graph by the identity permutation gives the same graph.
nodes.title: Relabelling by the identity

nodes.summary: For a statement $(G_0, G_1)$, the challenge $\alpha$ selects $G_1$ when $\alpha = 1$ and $G_0$ when $\alpha = 0$.
nodes.title: The graph a challenge asks about

nodes.summary: The graph-isomorphism protocol is complete: if $\varphi$ maps $G_0$ onto $G_1$, then for all prover coins $\pi$ and both challenges the honest answer is accepted. For $\alpha = 1$ the answer $\pi$ maps $G_1$ onto $H = \pi(G_1)$; for $\alpha = 0$ the answer $\pi \circ \varphi$ maps $G_0$ onto $\pi(\varphi(G_0)) = H$.
nodes.title: Completeness of the graph-isomorphism protocol

nodes.summary: For isomorphic graphs, the transcripts of the graph-isomorphism protocol with the honest verifier (uniform challenge) have exactly the distribution of the simulator that draws a uniform challenge $\alpha$ and a uniform permutation $\sigma$ and outputs $(\sigma(G_\alpha), \alpha, \sigma)$. This is perfect zero knowledge with respect to the honest verifier only; Goldreich, Micali and Wigderson's Theorem 2 proves…
nodes.title: Perfect honest-verifier zero knowledge of the graph-isomorphism protocol

nodes.summary: For isomorphic graphs, with any witness $\varphi$, and for each challenge $\alpha$, the honest pair (commitment, answer) of the graph-isomorphism protocol has exactly the distribution of the per-challenge simulator. For $\alpha = 1$ the pair is $(\pi(G_1), \pi)$; for $\alpha = 0$ it is $(\pi(G_1), \pi \circ \varphi) = (\sigma(G_0), \sigma)$ with $\sigma = \pi \circ \varphi$, which is uniform when $\pi$ is.
nodes.title: Perfect special honest-verifier zero knowledge of the graph-isomorphism protocol

nodes.summary: The graph-isomorphism protocol is specially sound with the extractor: from two accepting transcripts with the same commitment $H$ and different challenges, the extractor computes a permutation mapping $G_0$ onto $G_1$.
nodes.title: Special soundness of the graph-isomorphism protocol

nodes.summary: One round of the zero-knowledge proof of Goldreich, Micali and Wigderson for graph isomorphism, for simple graphs on a vertex type $V$. A statement is a pair $(G_0, G_1)$; a witness is a permutation $\varphi$ of $V$ that maps $G_0$ onto $G_1$. The prover draws a uniform permutation $\pi$ and commits to $H = \pi(G_1)$. On the challenge $\alpha$ it answers $\pi$ if $\alpha = 1$ and $\pi \circ \varphi$ if…
nodes.title: The graph-isomorphism protocol as a Sigma protocol

nodes.summary: For a statement $(G_0, G_1)$ and a challenge $\alpha$, the simulator draws a uniform permutation $\sigma$ and outputs the pair $(\sigma(G_\alpha), \sigma)$, computed from the two graphs alone, where $G_\alpha$ is the graph selected by $\alpha$.
nodes.title: The per-challenge simulator

nodes.summary: For isomorphic graphs with witness $\varphi$, every verifier $V^*$ (its challenge any function of the prover's graph $H$ and of its coins) and every test $T$ of its view, one attempt of the simulator (guess $\alpha'$, send $\sigma(G_{\alpha'})$ for a uniform $\sigma$, keep the attempt if $V^*$ asks $\alpha'$) succeeds and passes $T$ with probability exactly half the probability that the real view passes $T$.
nodes.title: One rewinding attempt for the graph-isomorphism protocol

nodes.summary: If $G_0$ and $G_1$ are not isomorphic, every cheating prover with coins in a finite type, committing to a graph and then answering the uniform challenge, is accepted by the verifier of one round of the graph-isomorphism protocol with probability at most $\tfrac12$.
nodes.title: Soundness error `1/2` per round

nodes.summary: If $G_0$ and $G_1$ are not isomorphic, every adaptive cheating prover, whose graph and answer in each round may depend on its coins and on the earlier challenges, passes all $m$ rounds of the graph-isomorphism protocol with probability at most $2^{-m}$.
nodes.title: Soundness error `2^{-m}` over `m` rounds

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
